text:
alex: seeing a flurry of ALB target removals in us-west-2 starting ~03:07 UTC, lots of readiness fail -> 503s.
linda: same, only for edge pods serving inference prewarm traffic. spike correlated with egress IPs rotating on those nodes.
sre-bot: [ALB] Target deregistration: targetId=i-0abcd, reason=health check failed, code=503
mike: logs show probe TCP->127.0.0.1:8081 timing out, but the app is up. kubelet probe shows SYN retransmits on node.
ops: this looks like ephemeral SNAT port churn — when egress IP changes we saw TCP resets during the brief rebind window.
emma: can we confirm conntrack entries? run:
```
sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.0.2.0/24 | tail -n 20
```
alex: did that, saw a ton of TIME_WAIT/ASSURED entries, and a small window where src port reused -> probe packets never reach pod.
linda: ALB healthchecks are coming from a fixed IP set; if node SNAT mapping flips, the reply path can break briefly and ALB marks unhealthy quickly.
mike: healthcheck config: interval=5s, unhealthy_threshold=2 -> 10s to mark. We had many nodes flapping so targets dropped.
ops: short-term mitigation: increase unhealthy_threshold to 5 and interval to 10s on the ALB target group to avoid transient removals.
emma: long-term: reduce SNAT churn. two options:
- use IP target type (NLB with IP targets) to avoid node SNAT
- set externalTrafficPolicy: Local on Service + preserve client IP to avoid SNAT for external traffic
alex: externalTrafficPolicy: Local would require ensuring pods run on nodes with ENIs for that subnets — capacity impact.
linda: also found kube-proxy restarting around same time on some nodes; that + CNI reattach causes transient route changes.
ops: action items: 1) bump ALB healthcheck to 10s/5 until fix rolled 2) investigate kube-proxy restart cause 3) evaluate switching to IP target NLB for critical edge pool
mike: quick test script I ran for repro:
```
# simulate egress IP rotate
ip route change default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0
sleep 0.5
# run curl healthcheck
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8081/health
```
alex: when route flipped within 200-400ms probes occasionally returned connection reset.
emma: I'll open a short-lived runbook and a PR to adjust target-group to 10s/5. assign to ops and network.
deploy-bot: deployment roll ics edge/pool-a updated healthcheck props by emma (PR #4721)
linda: monitoring tweak: add alert if target dereg count > 3 within 15m for same target group to catch regression earlier.
ops: putting the mitigation in place now, will monitor for the next 2 hours and report back.
alex: thanks team — if we still see flaps after kube-proxy fix we should prioritize IP target NLB for the edge fleet.
